# FDG9053

> DO provide a regular CLR property and public static read-only field storing an instance of `System.Windows.DependencyProperty` for each dependency property.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.3.1 Dependency Property Design.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9053
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Declare the dependency property field '{0}' public static readonly

FDG9053 reports a static field of type DependencyProperty initialized with DependencyProperty.Register or RegisterAttached that is not declared public static readonly; the private field of the FDG9058 example is reported. Whether the class has the CLR property is not checked, since the examples of FDG9055 and FDG9056 leave it out, and fields initialized otherwise (the DependencyProperty of a read-only property, taken from its key) are not seen, so coverage is partial. Making the field public or read-only changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

```csharp
public class TextButton : DependencyObject {

  public string Text {
    get { return (string)GetValue(TextProperty); }
    set { SetValue(TextProperty, value); }
  }

  public static readonly DependencyProperty TextProperty =
    DependencyProperty.Register(
      "Text",
      typeof(string),
      typeof(TextButton));
}
```
